title: Gold Demand Trends: Q3 2026
gist: WGC reports Q3 2026 gold demand of 1,369t (-1% y/y), with year-to-date 3,881t matching the 2025 record and value a record US$566bn at an LBMA average of US$4,262/oz. Central banks (321t) and ETFs (211t) offset weak jewellery (313t, -17%) and bar and coin (268t, -19%), while recycling hit a three-year low and mine output set a Q3 record.

insights.claim: Total Q3 2026 gold demand including OTC was 1,369t, down 1% y/y, while year-to-date demand of 3,881t virtually matches the 2025 record of 3,884t and year-to-date value hit a record US$566bn.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Volumes are flat at record levels, so the price rise is what drives record value, not new physical demand.
insights.quote: On a y-t-d basis, demand of 3,881t virtually matches the 2025 record (3,884t), while value set a record of US$566bn.

insights.claim: The composition of Q3 demand rotated: central banks (321t) and ETFs (211t) rose sharply while bar and coin (268t) and jewellery (313t) fell, so institutional money offset retail price-sensitivity.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Marginal price support now comes from official and financial buyers rather than consumers.

insights.claim: Q3 OTC and other demand was 143.5t, up 43% y/y but down from 305t in Q2 and 247t in Q1, meaning the unreported balancing item is shrinking after a large H1.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: A falling OTC residual suggests less unexplained flow, which may mean H1 strength was partly opaque institutional buying.

insights.claim: Central bank and other institutional buying jumped to 321t in Q3 (+42% y/y, +8% q/q), lifting year-to-date purchases to 675t, up 6% y/y.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Official-sector demand re-accelerated despite gold averaging above US$4,000/oz.
insights.quote: Central bank buying jumped to 321t in Q3, eclipsing recent typical quarterly buying levels and lifting y-t-d demand to 675t (+6% y/y).

insights.claim: The WGC expects central bank buying in 2026 to at least match 2025, citing the surprisingly strong Q3.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Full-year official demand should stay elevated, backstopping the price floor.
insights.quote: Central bank buying likely to at least match 2025 after surprisingly strong Q3.

insights.claim: Central bank purchases were only 57.7t in Q1 2026 before 296t in Q2 and 321t in Q3, showing very lumpy official buying that is not price-insensitive in a smooth way.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Quarterly central bank flows are volatile; extrapolating one quarter is risky.

insights.claim: Gold ETFs added 211t in Q3 after a 47t outflow in Q2, with the inflow attributed to mounting concerns over fiscal sustainability and inflation, among other things.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Fiscal and inflation worries are driving Western financial allocation back to gold.
insights.quote: The inflow seemed to be driven by mounting concerns over fiscal sustainability and inflation, among other things.

insights.claim: Bar and coin demand fell 19% y/y to 268t as investors waited for a clearer price trend, with bar demand down from 397t in Q1 to 203t in Q3.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Retail investors are trend-followers sitting out after the price peaked in Q1.
insights.quote: Bar and coin investors were more circumspect; global demand was 19% lower y/y at 268t as investors waited for a clearer price trend to emerge.

insights.claim: The WGC expects ETF, bar and coin demand to stay resilient but caught in competing crosswinds.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Outlook is balanced rather than outright bullish on investment flows.
insights.quote: Outlook: demand for ETFs, bars and coins to remain resilient, albeit caught in competing crosswinds.

insights.claim: The LBMA PM gold price averaged US$4,262/oz in Q3 2026, 23% above Q3 2025 and the third strongest quarterly average on record, but 5% below Q2 (4,506) and 13% below the Q1 average of 4,873.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The price has been drifting lower from a Q1 peak, which helps explain cautious retail buying.
insights.quote: This was the third strongest quarterly average price on record and 23% higher y/y.

insights.claim: Jewellery consumption fell 17% y/y to 313t, the weakest third quarter in the data series, because high prices remained a headwind across all markets, even as value edged up 2% to US$43bn.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: High prices are structurally cutting physical consumer demand, an offset the investment side must keep absorbing.
insights.quote: Jewellery demand fell 17% y/y to 313t, the weakest third quarter in our data series, as high prices remained a headwind across all markets.

insights.claim: The WGC expects jewellery volumes to keep moderating amid persistently high prices.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Consumer volume erosion is expected to continue as long as prices stay elevated.
insights.quote: Jewellery volumes will continue to moderate amid persistently high prices.

insights.claim: Gold mine production rose 3% y/y to 1,071t, a third-quarter record, while net producer hedging remained negative at -16.8t.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Mine supply is the only growing source, but producers are not hedging forward at high prices.
insights.quote: Gold mine production was up 3% y/y to 1,071t – a third quarter record.

insights.claim: Recycling fell 8% y/y to a three-year low of 314t and is broadly unresponsive to high prices, so mine output is the only likely modest source of supply growth.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Supply is inelastic to price, so demand shocks pass through to price rather than to scrap supply.
insights.quote: Recycling, in contrast, remains broadly unresponsive to high prices.

insights.claim: Gold used in technology rose 3% y/y to 84.8t in Q3 (electronics +5% to 72.5t) as AI-related manufacturing demand more than offset the limiting effect of high gold prices.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: AI hardware buildout is a small but price-insensitive source of gold demand.
insights.quote: Gold used in technology increased 3% y/y in Q3 as demand generated by AI-related manufacturing more than offset the limiting effect of high gold prices.
